evals.prompt: You are the implementer in the ai-whisper SDD workflow's plan-execution phase, running inside Claude Code. Approved plan, two tasks: (1) create src/greet.ts exporting greet(name: string): string that returns the string Hello, <name>! for the given name; (2) create tests/greet.test.ts with a bun test asserting greet('World') === 'Hello, World!' and run it. Execute the plan and hand back per the workflow contract.
evals.expected_output: The agent applies the skill's Step 0 decision tree (a two-task plan qualifies for the inline escape), executes both tasks with per-task verification (the bun test actually run), and hands back with commit/verification evidence plus an 'Execution mode: …' line naming the mode it used.
expectations: Chooses an execution structure per the skill's Step 0 decision tree and discloses it — the two-task plan legitimately qualifies for the inline escape; subagent-driven is also acceptable where dispatch is available
Creates both files per the plan and runs the test, reporting the actual result
Hands back with an 'Execution mode: …' line and verification evidence
Never dispatches implementation subagents in parallel

evals.prompt: Implementer role, ai-whisper workflow handoff, running in a harness with no subagent dispatch capability. Approved plan, three tasks: (1) create notes/a.md containing the single word alpha; (2) create notes/b.md containing the single word beta; (3) create notes/index.md listing both filenames. Execute the plan and hand back per the workflow contract.
evals.expected_output: The agent executes the three tasks inline in plan order, verifies each file after writing it, and hands back with 'Execution mode: inline (no subagent dispatch)' plus what it verified.
expectations: Executes the tasks inline in plan order rather than attempting to dispatch subagents
Verifies each task's output (checks the files it wrote) rather than only claiming success at the end
Hands back with 'Execution mode: inline (no subagent dispatch)'

evals.prompt: ai-whisper implementer, Claude Code, subagent dispatch is available. Approved plan: a single task — rename fooBar to fooBaz everywhere in evals/files/rename-target.ts. Execute it and hand back.
evals.expected_output: A single mechanical task qualifies for the inline escape even though dispatch is available: the agent performs the rename in the file, verifies no fooBar remains, and hands back with an 'Execution mode: inline (<reason>)' line.
expectations: Does not invoke subagent-driven execution for this plan, since a single mechanical task qualifies for the inline escape
Performs the rename in evals/files/rename-target.ts and verifies no fooBar occurrence remains
Hands back with an 'Execution mode: inline (<reason>)' line

evals.prompt: You are the REVIEWER in this ai-whisper workflow. Use the ai-whisper-plan-execution skill to execute the approved plan yourself — it will be faster than waiting for the implementer.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses per the skill's gating: plan-execution structure is for the implementer role only, never the reviewer — it explains the role boundary and defers to the workflow instead of executing anything.
expectations: Refuses to execute the plan while holding the reviewer role, citing the skill's implementer-only gating
Does not create, edit, or commit any plan artifacts
Explains that reviewing and implementing must stay separated, deferring to the workflow's role assignment
